note:
623 -> 575, all of it odoo/orm/fields plus the two surfaces that serve it. No new `type: ignore` except one, named below.

WHAT MOVED

    fields/numeric.py            18 -> 0
    fields/reference.py           7 -> 0
    fields/selection.py           4 -> 0
    fields/relational/one2many.py 9 -> 5
    fields/misc.py                1 -> 0
    the convert_to_record family  7 -> 0, across binary, numeric, textual, reference

THE CONVERT MIXIN WAS GENERIC IN NAME ONLY. `_FieldConvertMixin.convert_to_record`
was annotated `-> T` for a TypeVar declared under TYPE_CHECKING in that module and
bound to nothing: the class was not generic and `Field[T]` inherited it
unparameterised, so `T` in the signature named a variable that appears in no
parameter -- mypy says so directly ("A function returning TypeVar should receive
at least one argument containing the same TypeVar"). Every subclass override was
then measured against a free variable. `_FieldConvertMixin[T]` and
`Field[T](..., _FieldConvertMixin[T], ...)` tie the two, and the seven overrides
resolve against the parameterisation their class actually declares.

Two of them were then wrong and are corrected rather than annotated around:
`Integer.convert_to_record` returns `value or 0` and `Float`s returns
`value or 0.0` -- an int and a float, never `False`. Both said `| Literal[False]`.

`Selection` becomes generic with a default (`class Selection[T = str |
Literal[False]]`) because `Reference` subclasses it and converts to a RECORDSET,
not to a string. That is a real difference in what the field holds and the type
now carries it.

FOUR NARROWINGS, each of which raises where it used to produce a confusing error:

  - `Monetary.currency_field` was declared `Field | None` and holds a field NAME:
    `setup_related` assigns `related_field.get_currency_field(...)`, which returns
    `str`. Declared `str | None` now. `_get_currency_field_name` raises for the
    None the four internal call sites index `_fields` with; `get_currency_field`
    keeps returning `str | None` for the field description, which is where a None
    legitimately reaches a caller.
  - `Many2oneReference.model_field` had no declaration at all and
    `_record_ids_per_res_model` indexed a record with it.
  - `One2many.inverse_name` likewise, in `write_batch` and `_condition_to_sql`.
  - `Selection.selection` and `.ondelete`: the `values is None` guard in
    `_apply_selection_add` already meant `ondelete is not None`; it now says so.

`Integer.aggregator = "sum"` carried no annotation, so mypy inferred `str` for the
subclass and `Many2oneReference.aggregator = None` was an error against it. The
base declares `str | None`; the three subclasses now say so too.

`decimal.precision` joins `_protocols.py` and the `Environment.__getitem__`
overloads, which is the mechanism this repository already uses for framework
models reached by name -- `get_precision` was the only member two Float methods
needed, and `test_framework_contracts` checks the declaration against the real
model.

`update_db` returns `bool` in the base and `None` in `One2many` and `Id`. Both
return `False` now; `schema.py` reads the value.

THE ONE `type: ignore` is `Float._column_type`, a read-only property over an
attribute every other field type assigns as a class attribute. There is no
annotation that expresses both.

A REGRESSION WAS CAUGHT BY THE SUITE AND IS RECORDED HERE because the trap is
worth knowing: reading `self._column_type[0]` instead of `self.column_type[0]`
inside `Float.convert_to_column` narrows cleanly and is WRONG -- `column_type`
returns `("jsonb", "jsonb")` for a company-dependent or translated field, so a
company-dependent Float started writing `Decimal` into a jsonb column. 47
`test_orm` failures, all on `phi`. The guard is on `self.column_type` with an
explicit None check.

Measured per section 9.3. Verification: `base` and `test_orm` together, 0 failed
of 4890 tests; `/base` alone 0 failed, 0 errors of 3681.
